newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs shrug off fund buying to end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs shrug off fund buying to end mixed.

text.p: Persistant commercial selling offset early fund buying to push CME hog futures down for losses late while thinly traded deferreds held gains. Pork bellies continued to trade mixed in local trade and ended lower in light dealings, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.325 cent per lb lower to 0.800 higher with July off most at 81.9235 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.225 to 0.875 lower with off the least at 81.425 cents.
Expectations of steady to weak cash hog markets Friday and possible weakness carrying over into next week weighed on hog futures and offset early technical fund buying, traders said.

Fund buying was most evident in August but commercial selling interest also developed on growing concern over less-than-expected exports to Japan. Exports may not increase until August or September rather than in June and July as had been expected after the Taiwan pork export ban, sources said.
Besides large stocks of pork in frozen storage in Japan, the current exchange rate makes it expensive for them to buy pork at this time, sources noted.
"It's just too expensive right now for Japan to step up their buying" of U.S. pork," said Dave Maher from Securities Corporation of Iowa.

USDA cited in its monthly Livestock, Dairy and Poultry report that a high U.S. dollar made imports from the U.S. relatively expensive in Japan. Another factor was lackluster demand due to high prices and food safety concerns that cut demand, USDA said the report.

Rand Financials bought August late before turning seller along with Cargill Investor Services. In hog options, Rand sold the July 82 straddle while commission houses bought August 76 puts and sold July 82 to 86 calls, pit sources said.
Pork belly futures trade remained dominated by locals as the market awaited the USDA Cold Storage report, traders said.

Local selling ran into underlying support generated by an expected bullish report which caused them to cover shorts at times and run prices up for gains. But the sold again late when hog futures retreated, they said.

Analyst estimates on the Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses as of May 31 ranged from 53.7 to 57.7 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.
